correctness.rationale: For an n-element first order, precisely n-1 ordered reference-successor edges exist. Nine or sixteen distinct profiles therefore force n≥10 or n≥17, respectively. In the explicit 10- and 17-point triples, each listed supplementary order is a bijection of the correct finite domain, and direct relational evaluation gives every status pair exactly once (full tables in RESULT.md, independently reconstructed by checker.py). Adding elements at the terminal end of all three orders preserves the old reference and supplementary adjacent/gap statuses, giving every n above each threshold. The formulas are finite conjunctions of existential two-variable clauses of quantifier rank two; no enumerative assertion is used to prove infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: The object is a natural rank-two finite-model test: local predecessor/successor signatures of three independent spanning paths on one reference successor relation. Quantifier rank two can require every local mask to occur. Exact finite spectra 10..∞ and 17..∞ exhibit the structural resource cost (seven vertices) of distinguishing opposite orientations of nonadjacent pairs, an expressivity boundary studied in the motivating logic papers. The result supplies two complete deterministic extremal models and uniform margin constraints usable as finite-model benchmarks, with no claim of a general small-model theorem.
